name: Limited lateral approach for proximal femoral implant insertion
corridor: Lateral window through fascia lata and vastus lateralis onto the lateral proximal femur, aligned with the femoral-neck axis for screws or a side plate

positioning.text: Position so closed reduction can be held and the lateral proximal femur imaged; the limb must remain accessible for a neck-axis-aligned lateral incision.

surface_landmarks.text: Mark the greater trochanter, femoral shaft, and the femoral-neck axis; a guide wire laid on the anterior hip and checked on the image intensifier locates the screw entry and the proximal end of the incision.

incision.text: For multiple screws, center a slightly posterior lateral incision on the neck-axis line. For a two-hole 135° sliding hip screw, begin a few centimeters proximal to the palpable greater trochanter and extend about 10 cm distally; a 95° blade plate needs a longer distal incision.

superficial_interval.text: Incise the iliotibial band distal to the greater trochanter in line with the skin, posterior to tensor fasciae latae so that muscle is not injured.

deep_interval.text: Incise vastus lateralis fascia, retract the muscle anteriorly or split atrophic fibers, and expose only enough lateral femur for hardware; bulky muscle can be reflected anteriorly through an added proximal transverse limb.

layers.text: Skin, subcutaneous tissue, iliotibial band, vastus lateralis, and the lateral femoral cortex.

structures_at_risk.text: The first perforating vessels typically lie more than 5 cm distal to the vastus lateralis ridge; careless division causes persistent bleeding. No named nerves are encountered until those vessels are reached.

danger_zones.text: Anticipate and control perforators before exposing more than 5 cm below the inferior border of the greater trochanter, especially beyond a short DHS plate.

retraction_hazards.text: Use limited Hohmann retraction and expose only the lateral surface needed for the implant; do not avulse perforators by uncontrolled posterior retraction.

exposure.text: Gives enough lateral proximal-femur surface for screws, a sliding hip screw, a blade plate, or a trochanteric stabilizing plate after proximal extension.

limitations.text: The standard window is for implant insertion after closed reduction; a femoral-neck fracture that needs direct reduction requires proximal-anterior extension into the gluteus medius–tensor interval.

extensions.text: Extend proximally through fascia lata onto the trochanter and gluteus medius insertion for a trochanteric stabilizing plate, or proximally and anteriorly toward the ASIS into the gluteus medius–tensor interval with a labrum-sparing capsulotomy for open neck reduction.

indications.text: Used to insert lateral fixation devices after closed reduction of proximal femoral fractures.

closure.text: Repair fascia lata and close subcutaneous tissue and skin after hemostasis of any divided perforators.

complications.text: Approach-related complications include perforator bleeding and hematoma, and labral injury if an anterior capsular extension is made carelessly.

procedure_applications.condition: Closed reduction is followed by extramedullary fixation with a sliding hip screw, blade plate, or similar lateral implant
Multiple screws or a side-plate construct is inserted from a lateral window after closed reduction

questions.question: How is the proximal end of a sliding-hip-screw incision located?
questions.answer: Lay a guide wire on the anterior hip, confirm it on the image intensifier along the neck axis, and start the incision where that line meets the lateral skin.

questions.question: Where are the first perforating vessels relative to the greater trochanter?
questions.answer: About 5 cm distal to the vastus lateralis ridge at the inferior border of the greater trochanter.

questions.question: Why is the fascia lata incised posterior to tensor fasciae latae?
questions.answer: To avoid injuring the tensor, which lies anteriorly between layers of the fascia.
